question: Should OpenClaw adopt a process-wide `OPENCLAW_LOCALE` selector plus a checked, owner-declared localization coverage manifest as core release-governance contracts for the localization series?
rationale: This choice determines a durable environment-variable API, release-gating automation, and cross-surface ownership boundary; correctness tests cannot decide whether that permanent product and maintenance commitment is desired.

options.title: Sponsor the staged core contract
options.body: Approve the selector and owner-declared coverage model, land the prerequisite foundation PRs first, then rebase this PR to its governance-only boundary.

options.title: Narrow the scope
options.body: Keep localization improvements surface-local and remove the repository-wide selector or release-gating manifest until maintainers define a smaller supported contract.

options.title: Pause the series
options.body: Defer the governance layer until the localization RFC and ownership model receive broader maintainer agreement.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the staged core contract
recommendation.body: Approve the selector and owner-declared coverage model, land the prerequisite foundation PRs first, then rebase this PR to its governance-only boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the proposal and can clarify its intended contract, although approval should come from the relevant current-main owners.
